# KINGAI OS

Official OS site: https://os.kingai.work
KINGAI main site: https://www.kingai.work
Repository: https://github.com/kingaiwork/KINGAIOS
Documentation: docs/INDEX.md
Verified status: docs/STATUS.md
Platform matrix: docs/PLATFORMS.md
Roadmap: docs/ROADMAP.md
Business and partnership: vip@kingai.work

Project: KINGAI OS
Architecture: D5 Sovereign Distributed Intelligence Operating System
Status: Alpha Runtime Foundation / Pre-Alpha
Source version: 0.1.0-dev
Base technology: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS technology base plus KINGAI-owned intelligence, governance, runtime, security, update, recovery, desktop and distribution layers
Primary principles: AI-native, Agent-native, Local-first, Secure-by-default, Model-neutral, Cloud-neutral, Controlled-evolution

Official editions:
- KINGAI OS Server
- KINGAI OS Desktop (personal computer / PC edition)
- KINGAI OS IoT / Edge
- KINGAI OS Container (Docker / OCI)

Desktop note:
- Desktop is the personal-computer edition.
- There is no separate PC build profile.

Current D5 runtime capabilities:
- local Unix-socket kingaid API
- Unix peer credential identity
- Agent Registry
- Capability Policy
- Approval Broker
- one-time approval consumption
- Task Graph persistence and lifecycle
- local-first Memory service
- provider-neutral Model Router
- append-oriented Audit
- sanitized Public Status
- CLI management for approval, memory, model and task operations

Approval security:
- approval is bound to Agent + Capability + Target Hash + Peer UID
- approval expires
- approval is single-use
- client JSON cannot self-assert Owner or Approved
- owner-level approval decisions are local UID 0 in the current developer implementation

Task states:
- created
- planning
- waiting
- waiting_approval
- running
- paused
- blocked
- failed
- completed
- cancelled

Desktop experiences:
- KINGAI Intelligence
- KINGAI Flow
- KINGAI Classic

Core architecture layers:
- KINGAI Intelligence
- KINGAI Governance
- KINGAI Execution Fabric
- KINGAI Secure Core
- Linux Kernel

Shared logical services:
- kingaid
- policy/capability governance
- approval broker
- task graph
- model fabric
- memory fabric
- audit
- update/recovery
- device integration

Execution adapters planned or staged:
- Native constrained executor
- OpenClaw
- MCP
- Codex-compatible tools
- Browser runtime
- Rootless containers
- Isolated VM/MicroVM backends

Platform targets:
Server:
- headless
- amd64 and arm64 rootfs paths
- current published Developer Preview: amd64 ISO

Desktop:
- personal computer / PC edition
- current architecture target: amd64
- Plasma 6 / KWin Wayland / SDDM / Qt 6

IoT / Edge:
- generic amd64 and arm64 image paths
- board-specific support requires validated Device Packs

Container:
- Docker / OCI
- amd64 and arm64 Buildx targets
- non-root kingaid by default
- no management TCP port exposed by default
- persistent /var/lib/kingai and /var/log/kingai

Verified OS engineering gate families include:
- Installer VM
- Desktop Live VM
- Server BIOS/UEFI VM
- A/B Update VM
- Recovery VM
- TUF Client
- Secure Boot VM
- Rollback Drill
- Recovery Drill

Not production-complete:
- constrained privileged Execution Broker
- final AppArmor/seccomp/Landlock agent sandbox policy
- Planner/task-step scheduler
- production OpenClaw/MCP/Codex adapters
- full M0-M6 memory retrieval/evolution pipeline
- production model-provider adapters
- production TUF repository
- production signing key custody and Secure Boot signing
- release branch governance
- production R2 release delivery
- board-specific bootable Edge Device Packs
- Stable lifecycle commitment

Distribution policy:
- Source code and release metadata: GitHub
- Large artifacts: KINGAI-controlled object storage / Cloudflare R2 when release credentials and gates are present
- Public download namespace: https://os.kingai.work/download
- Updates: https://os.kingai.work/updates
- Repository namespace: https://os.kingai.work/repo

Release channels:
- nightly
- dev
- beta
- rc
- stable

Legal note:
KINGAI OS is independently developed on an Ubuntu 26.04 LTS technology base and follows applicable open-source license and trademark requirements. Release claims are intentionally separated from source-code existence and CI verification.
